script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 6. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Medicine seems like magic—swallow a pill, feel better.  But most medicine isn't replacing your body's healing; it's supporting it.  Your body knows how to heal.

Antibiotics don't heal you—they kill bacteria. Your immune system handles the rest. Antivirals work differently, often stopping viruses from replicating. Medicine provides reinforcements for battles your body is already fighting. Many medicines modulate—they turn processes up or down.  Pain relievers reduce inflammation.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Healing usually means supporting natural processes.  Medicine teaches that your body has remarkable healing ability.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Healing Partnership - Support Your Body.

Here's your activity: Next time you take medicine, consider what it's actually doing: fighting invaders, reducing inflammation, or replacing something missing. Medicine is a partnership with your body's healing systems. What else can you do to support those systems? This helps you see medicine as supporting natural healing.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how medicine heals can be applied to healing partnership - support your body. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
